newsitem.title: INDIA: India 1997/98 export scenario bleak, says NatWest.
newsitem.headline: India 1997/98 export scenario bleak, says NatWest.

text.p: India's export prospects during 1997/98 (April-March) are bleak because of weak global demand, NatWest Securities said.
"Exporters are feeling bullish owing to the fiscal incentives in the FY1998 budget and the falling cost of borrowings," it said in a research report.

It said the export councils of the major items of export -- gems, jewellery, textiles and leather accounting for more than 40 percent of total exports -- still expect a growth of 15-20 percent during the current year.
"However, we feel that India's export outlook remains bleak largely because of weak global demand," it said.
The average export growth of most Asian countries has been above 20 percent in the beginning of 1996, but growth has been negative for most of these countries in 1997, it said.

"As speculators realise that export growth will remain weak and net inflows in FY1998 will be about 50 percent lower than in FY1997, the forex market should correct itself and the direction of the rupee dollar movement should get reversed," it said.
"Our forecasts of domestic consumption and manufacturing growth support a 15 percent growth in total imports in FY1998."
NatWest said it expected the merchandise trade deficit to further widen by $3.5 billion in FY1998 compared with FY1997.
"Hence, even if the inflows on the capital account remain strong, net inflows will be moderated in FY1998," it added.
Moderate net inflows will help the Reserve Bank of India to meet its M3 target for the year, it said.
"Our BOP (balance of payments) projections show that net inflows of about $2.0 billion in FY1998 will be compatible with the RBI's M3 growth projections," it said.

"Net inflows are likely to be somewhat lower than implied by the M3 growth projections of the RBI, but its large buildup of reserves will allow the central bank to preempt any sharp fall in the Indian rupee," NatWest said.
This would help the RBI to contain M3 growth to 16 percent in FY1998 against its target of 15.0-15.5 percent, it added.
